MetricHints.impressions: How many times the Pin appeared on screen — in the feed, search or on boards. One person can count several times.
MetricHints.saves: How many times the post was saved — to a board on Pinterest, or to saved items on Instagram.
MetricHints.pinClicks: How many times the Pin was opened or clicked — on or off Pinterest, including clicks to your site.
MetricHints.outboundClicks: How many times people went from the Pin to your website or shop via its link.
MetricHints.followers: Followers of the account right now — not for the period. Changes are tracked since Adelie started collecting.
MetricHints.views: How many times the account's content was played or displayed — posts, Reels, stories. An Instagram metric, not the same as Pinterest impressions.
MetricHints.engagements: All interactions with the content: likes, comments, saves, shares, replies.
MetricHints.newFollowers: How many people followed in the period. Instagram gives this only for the last 30 days.
MetricHints.reach: How many different accounts saw the post at least once.
MetricHints.shares: How many times the post was shared.
MetricHints.videoViews: How many times the pin’s video was viewed. Lifetime only: Pinterest does not report it per day.
MetricHints.orders: Number of shop orders in the period.
MetricHints.revenue: What buyers paid, without the sales tax Etsy remits itself. Etsy fees are not subtracted.

Invite.title: Connect {platform} to Adelie
Invite.lead: {name} from {workspace} invites you to connect your account so they can see its analytics.
Invite.leadNoName: {workspace} invites you to connect your account so they can see its analytics.

explain.pinterest: You will sign in on Pinterest and confirm access there. Adelie can only read profile, boards, pins and their statistics — it cannot post, edit or delete anything. Access can be revoked at any time in your Pinterest settings.
explain.instagram: You will sign in with Meta (Facebook / Instagram) and choose your professional Instagram account. Adelie can only read the profile, posts and their statistics — it cannot post, edit, delete or read messages. Access can be revoked at any time in your Instagram or Facebook settings.
explain.etsy: You will sign in to Etsy and confirm access there. Adelie can only read your shop, products and orders (amounts, items, country) — not buyers’ names, addresses or emails. It cannot change, publish or delete anything. You can revoke access any time in your Etsy settings.
explain.etsyWrite: You will sign in to Etsy and confirm access there. Adelie can read your shop, products and orders (not buyers’ names, addresses or emails) and edit or create products — only when a project member does it in Adelie. It cannot delete products or change orders or shop settings. You can revoke access any time in your Etsy settings.
explain.tiktok: You will sign in on TikTok and confirm access there. Adelie can only read the profile, its statistics and public videos with their statistics — it cannot post, edit or delete anything. Access can be revoked at any time in your TikTok settings.

Flipper.title: Flipper
Flipper.subtitle: What visitors do on your site: views, the funnel, traffic sources.
Flipper.noSitesText: Flipper works for sites connected to the project through a product feed. Connect a site and its install code appears here.
Flipper.enableText: We create the site id and the install code: two lines that go on your pages. Events start arriving right after that.
Flipper.noPermission: Flipper can be switched on by an owner, an admin or a manager.
Flipper.consentShare: {percent}% of events come from visitors who agreed
Flipper.consentHint: Without cookie consent Flipper counts views and unique visitors per day, but does not recognise a person across pages and days. The funnel and returning visitors count only those who agreed.
Flipper.visitorsHint: Each person is counted once a day: with consent by a persistent id, without it by an anonymous daily hash that does not link days. This is an estimate.
Flipper.funnel: Actions of visitors with a known source
Flipper.funnelHint: Visitors we could follow from page to page and whose source we know (they agreed to tracking; a visit with no referrer counts as Direct): how many of them reached each step. The percentage is of the previous step. Purchases are counted among them only; the Purchases tile shows all orders.
Flipper.noChannels: Sources appear when visits with utm labels or from other sites arrive.
Flipper.liveHint: The latest events, refreshed by themselves. ● the visitor agreed and is recognised, ○ anonymous (a hash for the day). Bots are not shown.
Flipper.noEvents: No events yet. Add the code to your site and open it.
Flipper.guideTitle: How to install and set up events

install.title: 1. Installation
install.lead: Add two lines to the head of every page (or once in a shared template). The first is a tiny stub so calls made before the script loads are not lost. The second is the script itself: it loads asynchronously, does not slow the site down and its errors never break the page.
install.next: In Next.js this goes in the root layout. Each domain has its own id. The mode of each site (full without a banner, or anonymous until consent) is switched in this cabinet above the code — the code on the site does not change. Copy the code with ?site=… in the address: that is how the mode reaches the site.
install.options: Options are attributes of the script tag: data-consent="granted" (do not wait for consent — see below), data-spa="false" (do not count route changes as page views), data-auto-pageview="false" (do not count the page view automatically), data-allow-params="page,sort" (which more address parameters may be sent; by default only utm and click ids), data-link-domains="gushka.world" (carry the visitor to your other domain), data-user-cookie="shop_uid" (the name of your own cookie with an opaque random visitor id: Flipper reads it and sends it with the events of visitors who agreed; or call flipper('identify', id). Use a random id, never an email or phone. It is stored only as a salted hash).

consent.title: 2. Cookie consent
consent.lead: By default Flipper is anonymous: it writes nothing to the browser, sets no cookie, and counts views and unique visitors per day. When the visitor agrees to analytics, call consent — then there is a persistent visitor, sessions, the funnel and the source they came from. If the visitor declines, call consent denied and Flipper stops sending.
consent.dnt: Flipper respects Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control: nothing is sent for such visitors. If your site runs on a basis that does not need consent, choose the mode Full, no banner in the cabinet (or put data-consent="granted" on the script tag — it wins over the cabinet).

events.title: 3. Shop events
events.lead: Five events follow the buyer’s way, from the category to payment. Names and properties are standard, so reports and the funnel work without extra set-up.
events.where: The simplest is to call them from your site’s code when the thing has really happened (not on the click: a click does not mean the product was added).
events.next: In Next.js a page view is tracked by a component, and add-to-cart in the button handler, after the cart accepted the product.

when.productView: a product page was opened (id is the article, the same as g:id in your feed)
when.addToCart: a product was added to the cart (after the cart answered)

events.htmlNote: Attributes work for simple values only. For a list of products use JavaScript.

props.category_id: The category id or slug, for example runners.
props.item_count: How many products are in items (counted by Flipper).
props.items: The products: a list of objects with id, name, price, quantity (up to 20).
props.item_id: The article — the same as g:id in your feed and the SKU in Etsy. This is how the product is matched across channels.
props.price: The unit price in the main currency unit (29000, not kopecks).
props.currency: The three-letter currency code: UAH, USD.
props.variant: The chosen option, for example the colour or size.
props.value: The total, price times quantity. Flipper counts it if you do not pass it.
props.coupon: The promo code, if one was entered.
props.transaction_id: The order number. Without it an order cannot be told apart from a repeat.

viewCategory.title: Category view
viewCategory.when: Fires when a category (catalogue) page has shown its products.
viewCategory.step1: Find the code that renders the category page.
viewCategory.step2: Call viewCategory once when the page opens, not on every re-render.
viewCategory.step3: Pass the category id and name; the list of products is optional.
viewCategory.mistake1: Calling it on every filter or sort change: one visit then looks like many.
viewCategory.mistake2: Sending the whole catalogue in items: only 20 products are kept.
viewCategory.test: Open a category with ?flipper_debug=1 and look in the browser console for an event line, then find ViewCategory in Live events.

productView.title: Product view
productView.when: Fires when a product page has shown the product. This is the most important event: top products and the funnel are built from it.
productView.step2: Call productView when the product is loaded.
productView.step3: Pass the article as id — exactly as it is in the feed.
productView.mistake1: Passing the database id instead of the article: the product will not match Etsy and the other site.
productView.mistake2: Price in kopecks or with a currency sign: send a plain number.
productView.test: Open a product page with ?flipper_debug=1: item_id must equal the article. In Top products the product appears with its name.

addToCart.title: Added to cart
addToCart.when: Fires after the cart has accepted the product.
addToCart.step1: Find the handler of the Add to cart button.
addToCart.step2: Call addToCart after the cart answered successfully.
addToCart.step3: Pass the product and the quantity.
addToCart.mistake1: Calling it on the click: if the cart refuses, the event is wrong.
addToCart.mistake2: Forgetting the quantity when more than one unit is added.
addToCart.test: Press the button: a new AddToCart with value appears in Live events.

beginCheckout.title: Checkout started
beginCheckout.when: Fires when the buyer starts checkout: presses Checkout in the cart or opens the checkout page.
beginCheckout.step1: Choose one place: the cart button or the checkout page.
beginCheckout.step2: Call beginCheckout with the cart lines.
beginCheckout.step3: Send the currency and the promo code if there is one.
beginCheckout.mistake1: Calling it in both places: every checkout is counted twice.
beginCheckout.mistake2: Calling it on every change of the delivery form.
beginCheckout.test: Go to checkout: BeginCheckout appears with item_count and value.

purchase.title: Purchase
purchase.when: Fires once when the order is paid. It closes the funnel and gives revenue.
purchase.step1: Choose the moment of payment: the payment callback on the server, or the thank-you page.
purchase.step2: Call purchase with the order number and the lines.
purchase.step3: Make sure it is sent once per order.
purchase.mistake1: Sending it again when the thank-you page is reloaded: guard it with the order number.
purchase.mistake2: Sending it for an unpaid order. Prefer the moment the payment is confirmed.
purchase.test: Make a test order: one Purchase with the order number appears.

events.ga4: Already send events to Google Analytics 4 (gtag or Tag Manager)? Then you do nothing: Flipper itself takes view_item_list, view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout and purchase from dataLayer and turns them into the events below. The only condition: item_id in these events must be the article (the same as g:id in your feed). Do not also call the same events by hand — they would be counted twice. To switch this off, put data-datalayer="false" on the script tag. The cards below are for sites without GA4 events.

attributes.title: 4. No code: data attributes
attributes.lead: For buttons and links you can do without JavaScript: add the attributes and a click on the element sends the event.
attributes.note: All data-flipper-* attributes become properties of the event: data-flipper-item-id becomes item_id. Numbers are recognised automatically. Handy for simple sites and site builders.

domains.title: 5. Two domains
domains.lead: Each domain is a separate site with its own id, so markets (hryvnia and dollars) are counted apart. So that a visitor who moves from one of your domains to the other is not counted as two people, put the other address in data-link-domains: links between the domains carry the visitor id (only with their consent), and on the second domain it is picked up and removed from the address.
domains.geo: If you have a geo redirect (for instance gushka.world → gushka.ua for Ukrainian IPs), make sure it keeps the address parameters: then utm labels are not lost and the source stays the original one.

sources.title: 6. Traffic sources
sources.lead: The source comes from the address the visitor arrived on (utm labels and click ids: gclid, fbclid, ttclid, epik, msclkid), and without them from the site they came from. An example link for a Pinterest post:
sources.rules: Write values in lower case, without spaces, the same for one source (always pinterest). Do not add labels to links inside your site. Source, medium and channel (Organic Social, Paid Search, Email, Referral, Direct…) are stored separately.

check.title: 8. Checking
check.lead: Open a page of the site with the parameter flipper_debug=1: every event appears in the browser console. Then look at “Live events” on this page.
check.problems: No events? Check: the script loaded (Network tab, the request to flipper.js), the collect request returned 204, the site is opened from an allowed domain, an ad blocker has not blocked the script.

server.title: 7. Purchases from the server
server.lead: Send the purchase from your backend when the payment is confirmed. Create a key in the card Purchases from your server above, put it in the environment of your server (never in the browser code) and call the address below. Save the _fl_v cookie when the order is created, so the purchase can be joined to the visitor and the channel; without it the purchase still counts, just with no channel. If you have your own opaque visitor id, pass it as user_id: the purchase is joined to that visitor’s earlier visits even when the _fl_v cookie was not saved.
server.after: The answer says created, or duplicate if this order was already reported (so a webhook, a poll and a cron job may all call it). The time of payment may be up to 7 days old. Errors: 401 wrong key, 400 the field named in error, 429 too many calls.

Flipper.modeHint: Anonymous: until the visitor agrees, nothing is stored in their browser and people are counted by a daily hash. Full: visitors are recognised at once, without a consent banner (your decision for this site). The change reaches the site within minutes — the code on the site stays the same.
Flipper.serverHint: When the browser may never return after paying (the bank closes its window), your server reports the purchase itself once the payment is confirmed. It is counted once per order and joined to the visitor’s channel. Authenticated by a secret key: keep it on the server only.
Flipper.serverRegenerate: The old key will stop working at once. Continue?
Flipper.serverShownOnce: Copy the key now: it is shown only once.
Flipper.srcHint: Visits count arrivals, also of those who did not agree. The steps after the visit (product views, cart, checkout) count the visitors who agreed, because only they can be followed, so for sites in anonymous mode they are lower. Purchases and revenue come from the server report. Click a channel to see its sources and campaigns. A purchase reported without a visitor id has no source: it is shown as Unattributed.
Flipper.srcDrill: Show the sources of this channel
Flipper.serverUrl: Address and method. The key goes in the header Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY; the body is JSON (see the guide below).
Flipper.chkHint: A person is followed from step to step only when they agreed, so these numbers are lower than the real traffic. Field names are counted, never what was typed.
Flipper.chkFieldsHint: Reached: the visitor went into the field and left it. Filled: it was not empty when they left. A big gap shows a field people give up on.
Flipper.kindHint: The type sets the starting goals, funnel and tabs: a shop has Checkout and products, a landing page does not. Changing it deletes no events.
Flipper.goalsHint: Goals are what counts as success for this site (a purchase, a download, a donation). They are counted from the events already collected, so a new or changed goal shows the past too.
Flipper.goalsNone: No goals yet. For a landing page add, e.g., “Download” — a click to the mod’s page.
Flipper.goalsHostHint: The domain the link leads to: nexusmods.com, steamcommunity.com, ko-fi.com. Subdomains count too.
Flipper.goalsPathHint: To count only a specific page: /ets2/mods/123. Empty — any click to that site.
Flipper.goalsPatternHint: A path on this site: /thanks. An asterisk matches anything: /download/* .
Flipper.goalsEventHint: A Flipper event: Purchase or the site’s own — flipper.track('Download').
Flipper.goalsValuedHint: Taken from the event’s value field (as in a purchase).
Flipper.goalsError: Check the fields: a name and a rule are needed (a site, a page starting with “/” or a latin event name).
Flipper.goalsFunnelHint: The steps a person takes towards the goal. Visitors who agreed to tracking are counted: only they can be followed from step to step.
Flipper.cartProductsHint: Products visitors added to the cart in the chosen period: how many times and by how many people.
